chunks: Muḥammad ibn Khālid al-Barqī narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about hiring, and he said:

It is sound; there is no harm in it, if he acts sincerely according to the extent of his ability. Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام had indeed hired out himself and stipulated, saying: If you wish, eight; and if you wish, ten. Then Allah, the Exalted, revealed concerning him:
That you hire yourself to me for eight pilgrimages (years); then if you complete ten, that is from your own accord.

key_terms.آجَرَ نَفْسَهُ: hired out himself for service or labor
key_terms.الْإِجَارَةِ: hiring, leasing, or employment by contract
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهَا: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.نَصَحَ: acted sincerely and faithfully in fulfilling the work

ai.seo_question: Is hiring oneself out for work permissible in Islam according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the permissibility of ijārah (hiring or employment) when carried out sincerely and according to one’s capacity. It cites the example of Mūsā ibn ʿImrān عليه السلام, whose service is referenced in the Qur'an, to show the legitimacy of contractual labor and agreed terms.
